Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Suspicious browser extension installation Installation Medium
Side-loaded / unsigned extensions, often masquerading as wallets, productivity tools.
ATT&CKT1176
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry DeviceRegistryEvents
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\","\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\","\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey,
          RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Browser Extension Installation via Registry
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0a
status: experimental
description: |
    Registry writes under the browser extension policy keys —
    administrative install of an extension. Often used by adware /
    info-stealers to bypass user-level extension controls.
references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1176

logsource:
    category: registry_event

detection:

        TargetObject|contains:
            - '\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\'

    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"

    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |

    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.

Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId

| order by TimeGenerated desc

The Hacker News
2026-06-11 10 use cases 4 techniques 7 kill-chain phases detected

For thirty years, vulnerability management ran on a buffer: the months between when a vulnerability was found and when someone could figure out how to weaponize it. The solution was straightforward enough; triage by severity, schedule the fix, validate, and move on. The buffer was what made that work. Today, that buffer is gone. AI didn't make your team slower. Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] FortiGate SSL-VPN / admin credential brute-force or spray from single source · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] First successful FortiGate admin/SSL-VPN login from never-seen ASN after failure burst · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Machine-cadence post-auth FortiGate CLI/API calls in single session (MCP-orchestrated)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound JSON-RPC or LLM-API egress from network appliance / edge device · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
FortiGate SSL-VPN / admin credential brute-force or spray from single source AIDelivery Medium
Detects the high-volume failed-then-successful FortiGate admin or SSL-VPN logins characteristic of the Feb 2026 MCP-orchestrated campaign in which an autonomous agent sprayed weak credentials against 2,516 queued appliances. Looks for one source IP touching many usernames or many devices with one or two attempts each, followed by a single success. Rationale: Article says actor 'queued 2,516 devices across 106 countries' with 'no zero-days needed, just weak credentials' via a custom MCP server. The detection grounds on multi-target single-source spray cadence specifically against FortiGate SSL-VPN/admin auth, not generic brute-force.
ATT&CKT1110.001 T1110.003 T1110.004
Data sourcesAuthentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Misconfigured customer VPN client retrying with cached bad password after policy change
  • Authorized BAS / red-team credential-spray runs against the same edge appliance
  • External vulnerability scanner (Qualys, Tenable) doing auth-checks against the SSL-VPN portal
  • NAT egress from a partner network where many users share one source IP and several fail MFA simultaneously
  • Mobile-device password change causing burst of 401s from a fleet of corporate phones
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in (dynamic(["<bas_egress_ip_1>", "<bas_egress_ip_2>"])) | where SourceUserName !startswith "redteam-"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm whether the source IP is on the approved BAS/red-team allow-list and whether any of the targeted usernames exist on the appliance; pull the actual admin/sslvpn log lines for the success event. 2) Contain: if not authorized, immediately disable the affected admin account, expire all SSL-VPN sessions for that user, block the source IP at the edge ACL, and force password reset + MFA enrollment. 3) Hunt: pivot on the source IP and ASN across all edge devices in the last 14 days; check for outbound connections from the FortiGate management plane to LLM/MCP endpoints; review config-change logs for the success window.
let WindowMin = 10m;
let FailedThreshold = 10;
let Failures = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(1d)
    | where RemotePort in (443, 10443, 8443) and InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("sslvpnd", "httpsd", "fgfm")
    | summarize Failed = count(), Users = make_set(InitiatingProcessAccountName), Devices = make_set(DeviceName) by RemoteIP, bin(Timestamp, WindowMin)
    | where Failed >= FailedThreshold;
Failures
| order by Timestamp desc
let WindowMin = 10m;
let FailedThreshold = 10;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Fortinet" and DeviceProduct in~ ("FortiGate", "Fortigate")
| where Activity has_any ("login", "ssl-vpn", "admin") or Message has_any ("login failed", "authentication failed", "ssl-vpn-login")
| extend Outcome = case(DeviceAction has "fail" or Message has_any ("failed", "denied"), "failure", DeviceAction has "success" or Message has "login success", "success", "unknown")
| summarize Failed = countif(Outcome == "failure"), Succeeded = countif(Outcome == "success"), Users = make_set(SourceUserName, 50), Hosts = make_set(DeviceExternalID, 50) by SourceIP, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where Failed >= FailedThreshold and Succeeded >= 1
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(linux.syslog OR cisco.firewall) (@source.product:(fortigate OR FortiGate) OR @network.client.port:(443 OR 10443)) (@evt.outcome:failure OR @msg:("login failed" OR "authentication failed" OR ssl-vpn-login)) -@network.client.ip:10.0.0.0/8
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Authentication.user) as distinct_users, dc(Authentication.dest) as distinct_dests, values(Authentication.user) as users, values(Authentication.dest) as dests from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=failure (Authentication.app=fortigate OR Authentication.app=sslvpn OR Authentication.app="FortiGate") by Authentication.src _time span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | where distinct_users>=10 OR distinct_dests>=10 OR count>=100 | join type=left src [| tstats `summariesonly` count as success_count, values(Authentication.user) as success_users, values(Authentication.dest) as success_dests from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=success (Authentication.app=fortigate OR Authentication.app=sslvpn) by Authentication.src | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`] | where isnotnull(success_count) | table _time src users dests distinct_users distinct_dests count success_count success_users success_dests
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Authentication.user) as distinct_users, dc(Authentication.dest) as distinct_dests, values(Authentication.user) as users, values(Authentication.dest) as dests from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=failure (Authentication.app=fortigate OR Authentication.app=sslvpn OR Authentication.app="FortiGate") by Authentication.src _time span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | where distinct_users>=10 OR distinct_dests>=10 OR count>=100 | join type=left src [| tstats summariesonly=false count as success_count, values(Authentication.user) as success_users, values(Authentication.dest) as success_dests from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=success (Authentication.app=fortigate OR Authentication.app=sslvpn) by Authentication.src | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`] | where isnotnull(success_count) | table _time src users dests distinct_users distinct_dests count success_count success_users success_dests
First successful FortiGate admin/SSL-VPN login from never-seen ASN after failure burst AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the post-spray foothold step from the Feb 2026 campaign: the first-ever successful FortiGate authentication from an ASN/geo that had only failures in the baseline window. AWS confirmed 600+ devices fell to this exact shape across 55+ countries. Rationale: Grounded in the article's 'AWS confirmed 600+ devices across 55+ countries' line and the kill-chain hint that first-time-seen ASN+success-after-failure-burst is the campaign's signature. Anti-baseline join is the canonical first-seen detection shape.
ATT&CKT1133 T1078
Data sourcesAuthentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Roaming admin connecting from a new hotel / airport ASN they've never used before
  • M&A integration where a newly-acquired sub-org logs in to the parent's appliance for the first time
  • MSP onboarding a new customer tenant from previously-unseen jump-host ASN
  • Carrier-grade-NAT shift moves a fleet of mobile clients to a new ASN block overnight
  • DR test from a backup site whose egress IP is not in the 30-day baseline
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in (dynamic(["<known_roaming_admin_ips>"])) | where SourceUserName !in~ ("msp-onboarding", "dr-test")
Response runbook
1) Triage: enrich the source IP with ASN/geo + threat-intel; pull the preceding 24 h of failures from the same /24; verify the account is genuinely admin/VPN with management access. 2) Contain: kill the active SSL-VPN tunnel, revoke session cookies, disable the account, and isolate the FortiGate management interface from public reach. 3) Hunt: look for config-change / `exec` CLI bursts from this session, outbound HTTPS from the appliance to LLM-API or unknown JSON-RPC endpoints, and any new admin or local user created in the same window.
let Lookback = 30d;
let Recent = 1h;
let KnownASN = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp between (ago(Lookback) .. ago(Recent))
    | where RemotePort in (443, 10443, 4433) and InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("sslvpnd", "httpsd")
    | summarize by RemoteIP;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(Recent)
| where RemotePort in (443, 10443, 4433)
| join kind=leftanti KnownASN on RemoteIP
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 30d;
let Recent = 1h;
let Baseline = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(Lookback) .. ago(Recent))
    | where DeviceVendor =~ "Fortinet" and DeviceProduct in~ ("FortiGate", "Fortigate")
    | where DeviceAction has "success" or Message has_any ("login success", "ssl-vpn-login success")
    | summarize by SourceIP;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Recent)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Fortinet" and DeviceProduct in~ ("FortiGate", "Fortigate")
| where DeviceAction has "success" or Message has_any ("login success", "ssl-vpn-login success")
| where SourceUserName has_any ("admin", "administrator") or Activity has_any ("ssl-vpn", "admin login")
| join kind=leftanti Baseline on SourceIP
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, DeviceExternalID, Activity, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(linux.syslog OR cisco.firewall) @source.product:(fortigate OR FortiGate) @evt.outcome:success (@msg:("login success" OR "ssl-vpn-login") OR @network.destination.port:(443 OR 10443)) @network.user.name:(admin OR administrator OR *vpn*)
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(Authentication.user) as users, values(Authentication.action) as actions from datamodel=Authentication where (Authentication.app=fortigate OR Authentication.app=sslvpn) earliest=-30d@d latest=-1h by Authentication.src_ip, Authentication.src_asn, Authentication.app | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | eventstats values(src_asn) as known_asns by app | eval is_baseline=1 | append [| tstats `summariesonly` count as recent_count, values(Authentication.user) as recent_users from datamodel=Authentication where (Authentication.app=fortigate OR Authentication.app=sslvpn) Authentication.action=success earliest=-1h by Authentication.src_ip, Authentication.src_asn, Authentication.app, _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | eval is_recent=1] | stats max(is_baseline) as seen_before, max(is_recent) as seen_recent, values(recent_users) as recent_users, values(recent_count) as recent_count, values(_time) as recent_time by src_asn, app | where seen_recent=1 AND isnull(seen_before) | table recent_time app src_asn recent_users recent_count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(Authentication.user) as users, values(Authentication.action) as actions from datamodel=Authentication where (Authentication.app=fortigate OR Authentication.app=sslvpn) earliest=-30d@d latest=-1h by Authentication.src_ip, Authentication.src_asn, Authentication.app | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | eventstats values(src_asn) as known_asns by app | eval is_baseline=1 | append [| tstats summariesonly=false count as recent_count, values(Authentication.user) as recent_users from datamodel=Authentication where (Authentication.app=fortigate OR Authentication.app=sslvpn) Authentication.action=success earliest=-1h by Authentication.src_ip, Authentication.src_asn, Authentication.app, _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | eval is_recent=1] | stats max(is_baseline) as seen_before, max(is_recent) as seen_recent, values(recent_users) as recent_users, values(recent_count) as recent_count, values(_time) as recent_time by src_asn, app | where seen_recent=1 AND isnull(seen_before) | table recent_time app src_asn recent_users recent_count
Machine-cadence post-auth FortiGate CLI/API calls in single session (MCP-orchestrated) AIInstallation Medium
Targets the Feb 2026 campaign's signature execution behaviour: an authenticated session that issues many FortiGate CLI/API actions sub-second apart — a cadence no human admin produces — because a custom MCP server is autonomously invoking a curated offensive-tool library against the appliance. Rationale: Article: 'bursts of FortiGate CLI/API calls (config read, diagnose, exec) spaced sub-second apart from a single session — a cadence no human admin produces.' Detection encodes that exact rate/burst signal at the session level rather than alerting on individual commands.
ATT&CKT1059 T1106
Data sourcesChange Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • FortiManager pushing a large policy bundle to the appliance during a scheduled change window
  • Backup / config-export tool (FortiAnalyzer collector, rConfig) pulling running-config via API on cron
  • Authorized BAS or pentest agent enumerating the appliance over the REST API
  • Ansible / Terraform deployment run that idempotent-replays hundreds of `config` blocks
  • Initial provisioning of a new appliance where the engineer pastes a multi-hundred-line config script
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in (dynamic(["<fortimanager_ip>", "<backup_collector_ip>", "<ansible_runner_ip>"]))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the session's source IP and admin account; check whether FortiManager / approved automation source the burst, and pull the actual command sequence. 2) Contain: terminate the active session, revoke the admin's API token, snapshot the running-config and diff against last-known-good, and block the source IP at the management ACL. 3) Hunt: pivot on the admin account for any new policies, route changes, local user creation, or VPN tunnels added in the burst; check egress from the appliance management plane to LLM/MCP endpoints.
let Window = 1m;
let BurstThreshold = 20;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort in (443, 22, 8443) and InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("httpsd", "sshd", "cli")
| summarize Calls = count(), FirstT = min(Timestamp), LastT = max(Timestamp) by RemoteIP, DeviceName, bin(Timestamp, Window)
| extend DurationSec = datetime_diff('second', LastT, FirstT), RatePerSec = todouble(Calls) / (todouble(datetime_diff('second', LastT, FirstT)) + 1)
| where Calls >= BurstThreshold and (RatePerSec >= 2.0 or DurationSec <= 10)
| order by Timestamp desc
let Window = 1m;
let BurstThreshold = 20;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Fortinet" and DeviceProduct in~ ("FortiGate", "Fortigate")
| where Activity has_any ("config", "exec", "diagnose", "api", "cli") or Message has_any ("exec ", "config ", "diagnose ", "/api/v2/")
| extend SessionKey = strcat(SourceIP, "|", SourceUserName, "|", DeviceExternalID)
| summarize Calls = count(), Cmds = make_set(Activity, 50), FirstT = min(TimeGenerated), LastT = max(TimeGenerated) by SessionKey, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DeviceExternalID, bin(TimeGenerated, Window)
| extend DurationSec = datetime_diff('second', LastT, FirstT)
| extend RatePerSec = todouble(Calls) / (todouble(DurationSec) + 1.0)
| where Calls >= BurstThreshold and (RatePerSec >= 2.0 or DurationSec <= 10)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(linux.syslog OR cisco.firewall) @source.product:(fortigate OR FortiGate) (@msg:(exec* OR config* OR diagnose* OR "/api/v2/") OR @evt.name:(config_change OR cli_command OR api_call))
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Change.object) as distinct_objects, values(Change.command) as commands, values(Change.object) as objects, min(_time) as first_t, max(_time) as last_t from datamodel=Change where (Change.vendor_product="FortiGate" OR Change.app=fortigate) by Change.user, Change.src, Change.session_id, _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(Change)` | eval duration_s=last_t-first_t, rate_per_s=count/(duration_s+1) | where count>=20 AND (rate_per_s>=2 OR duration_s<=10) | table _time user src session_id count distinct_objects duration_s rate_per_s commands objects
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Change.object) as distinct_objects, values(Change.command) as commands, values(Change.object) as objects, min(_time) as first_t, max(_time) as last_t from datamodel=Change where (Change.vendor_product="FortiGate" OR Change.app=fortigate) by Change.user, Change.src, Change.session_id, _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(Change)` | eval duration_s=last_t-first_t, rate_per_s=count/(duration_s+1) | where count>=20 AND (rate_per_s>=2 OR duration_s<=10) | table _time user src session_id count distinct_objects duration_s rate_per_s commands objects
Outbound JSON-RPC or LLM-API egress from network appliance / edge device AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the C2 channel from the Feb 2026 campaign: the custom MCP server brokering tasks between the LLM and compromised FortiGate fleet over HTTPS. Network appliances should never originate AI-API traffic; first-seen FQDN to anthropic / openai / bedrock / unknown JSON-RPC endpoints from edge gear is the tell. Rationale: Article: 'a custom MCP server running offensive tools autonomously' brokering between LLM and compromised devices. Detection ground-truths on the unique behavioural shape — edge appliance originating LLM-API HTTPS — which is essentially zero in any baseline. CloudWatch/VPC-Flow path was dropped because the article-specific telemetry lives on the FortiGate / proxy / DNS layer, not in CloudTrail; emitting an invented VPC-Flow query would be noise.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vendor support session where a FortiGate streams telemetry through an OpenAI-fronted vendor diagnostic chatbot
  • Legitimate internal SOAR / chatops integration on an appliance management host that genuinely calls an LLM
  • Captive-portal proxy on the appliance forwarding a user's browser session to an LLM provider (rare)
  • Future Fortinet firmware that ships its own AI assistant phoning home to a vendor LLM endpoint
  • DNS resolver on the appliance answering a recursive query for a downstream client (split-horizon misconfig)
Suppression filter
| where DestinationHostName !in~ ("telemetry.fortinet.com", "<approved_vendor_chatops_host>") | where SourceIP !in (dynamic(["<approved_soar_egress_ip>"]))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify which appliance and which management-plane process originated the connection; verify whether the destination FQDN is a known LLM endpoint and whether any vendor change ticket explains it. 2) Contain: block the destination FQDN/IP at the perimeter from all network-appliance source IPs, snapshot the appliance config and running processes, and rotate admin credentials and API tokens on that device. 3) Hunt: correlate with recent admin-login anomalies on the same appliance, look for matching outbound from peer appliances of the same model, and search for inbound JSON-RPC / unusual TLS-SNI patterns that could be the MCP control channel itself.
let LLMHosts = dynamic(["anthropic.com", "api.anthropic.com", "openai.com", "api.openai.com", "bedrock-runtime", "generativelanguage.googleapis.com", "api.mistral.ai", "api.together.xyz", "api.groq.com", "api.deepseek.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort == 443
| where RemoteUrl has_any (LLMHosts) or InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("sslvpnd", "httpsd", "miglogd", "fgfm", "forticron")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe", "msedge.exe", "firefox.exe", "brave.exe", "code.exe", "slack.exe", "teams.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let LLMHosts = dynamic(["anthropic.com", "api.anthropic.com", "openai.com", "api.openai.com", "bedrock-runtime", "generativelanguage.googleapis.com", "api.mistral.ai", "api.together.xyz", "api.groq.com", "api.deepseek.com"]);
let ApplianceVendors = dynamic(["Fortinet", "Palo Alto Networks", "Cisco", "Check Point", "SonicWall", "Juniper", "F5"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DeviceVendor in~ (ApplianceVendors)
| where DestinationPort == 443 or ApplicationProtocol has_any ("https", "ssl", "tls")
| where (isnotempty(DestinationHostName) and DestinationHostName has_any (LLMHosts)) or (isnotempty(RequestURL) and RequestURL has_any (LLMHosts)) or (isnotempty(DestinationDnsDomain) and DestinationDnsDomain has_any (LLMHosts))
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, DeviceExternalID, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain, RequestURL, Activity, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc
| union (
    ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (LLMHosts)
    | where SrcHostname has_any ("fgt", "fortigate", "palo", "asa", "ftd", "checkpoint", "srx", "bigip") or DvcHostname has_any ("fgt", "fortigate", "palo", "asa", "ftd", "checkpoint", "srx", "bigip")
    | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor=EventVendor, DeviceProduct=EventProduct, DeviceExternalID=DvcHostname, SourceIP=SrcIpAddr, DestinationIP=DstIpAddr, DestinationPort=int(null), DestinationHostName=DstHostname, DestinationDnsDomain=DnsQuery, RequestURL=tostring(""), Activity=tostring("dns_query"), Message=tostring("")
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents

| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc

| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

OceanLotus Hits Vietnam Investors With SPECTRALVIPER in FireAnt Attack

The Hacker News
2026-06-11 15 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The Vietnam-aligned threat actor known as OceanLotus has been attributed to two distinct campaigns that targeted domestic entities and stock investors with a backdoor known as SPECTRALVIPER. The campaigns involve a prolonged cyber espionage operation aimed at a Vietnamese infrastructure and transport construction corporation between mid-2024 and February 2026, as well as a supply chain attack

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] FireAnt Metakit.exe spawning setup.exe — malicious update download chain · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — OceanLotus Hits Vietnam Investors With SPECTRALVIPER in FireAnt Attack
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] SPECTRALVIPER DLL side-load — DtlCrashCatch.dll dropped/loaded from non-system path · [LLM] SPECTRALVIPER injection into OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe · [LLM] SPECTRALVIPER SHA1 IOC sightings — file write, process exec, image load · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] OceanLotus / SPECTRALVIPER C2 infrastructure callouts · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
FireAnt Metakit.exe spawning setup.exe — malicious update download chain AIDelivery High
Hunts the FireAnt Metakit supply-chain entry point where the legitimate Metakit.exe (the FireAnt stock-investor client) launches a tampered setup.exe pulled from the unsigned update server. ESET notes the version.xml at metakit.fireant.vn lacks integrity validation, so the legit client process becomes the parent of the OceanLotus downloader. Rationale: Pivot is the article-specific parent binary 'Metakit.exe' (FireAnt's client) — there is no legitimate reason for it to spawn a setup.exe out of a user-writable directory. Cross-checked with ESET's report and Elastic Security Labs' 2023 SPECTRALVIPER write-up which describes the same DLL side-loading pattern via 'legitimate' parent binaries (https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper). Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate FireAnt update after they finally implement signing (would still be unusual today)
  • FireAnt installer re-run by sysadmin during reimage to %Public%
  • Software-deployment tool wrapping Metakit.exe and calling setup.exe via PSAppDeployToolkit
  • Sandbox / dev machine running FireAnt sample for analysis
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessSignatureStatus != "Signed" or InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName !has "FireAnt"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the dropped setup.exe SHA256 and compare against the article's SHA1s; check the metakit.fireant.vn update URL the parent process resolved (DeviceNetworkEvents within ±10 min on same DeviceId). 2) Contain: network-isolate the host via Defender Live Response, kill Metakit.exe + setup.exe, preserve the binary for triage. 3) Hunt: pivot DeviceId across DeviceImageLoadEvents for DtlCrashCatch.dll loads in the next 24h and DeviceNetworkEvents to financemachinelearning.com / gatewayrvcenter.com — confirms the SPECTRALVIPER injection completed.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "Metakit.exe"
| where FileName =~ "setup.exe"
   or FolderPath has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\ProgramData\")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, SHA1,
          ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA256,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has "Metakit.exe"
| where TargetProcessName has "setup.exe"
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\ProgramData\")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName,
          ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256, SHA1
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: FireAnt Metakit.exe Spawning setup.exe From User-Writable Path
id: 1e63a4f2-7d8b-4c5a-a1c7-9d3e2f4b8c01
description: Detects FireAnt Metakit.exe (Vietnamese stock-investor client) spawning a child setup.exe — the SPECTRALVIPER staging chain used in the OceanLotus FireAnt Metakit supply-chain attack reported by ESET.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/oceanlotus-hits-vietnam-investors-with.html
  - https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper
author: ThreatHuntingNarwhal
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1204.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\Metakit.exe'
  selection_child:
    - Image|endswith: '\setup.exe'
    - Image|contains:
        - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
        - '\Users\Public\'
        - '\ProgramData\'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate Metakit auto-update if FireAnt eventually ships signed installers (verify update server cert)
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1) OR (source:windows.security @EventID:4688) (@ParentImage:(*\\Metakit.exe OR *\\metakit.exe OR *\\METAKIT.EXE) OR @ParentProcessName:(*\\Metakit.exe OR *\\metakit.exe)) (@Image:(*\\setup.exe OR *\\Setup.exe OR *\\SETUP.EXE) OR @NewProcessName:(*\\setup.exe OR *\\Setup.exe))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^Metakit\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\setup\.exe$/i OR regex("\\\\(AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp|Users\\\\Public|ProgramData)\\\\", field=ImageFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="Metakit.exe" AND (Processes.process_name="setup.exe" OR Processes.process_path IN ("*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*","*\\Users\\Public\\*","*\\ProgramData\\*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="Metakit.exe" AND (Processes.process_name="setup.exe" OR Processes.process_path IN ("*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*","*\\Users\\Public\\*","*\\ProgramData\\*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
SPECTRALVIPER DLL side-load — DtlCrashCatch.dll dropped/loaded from non-system path AIInstallation High
Catches the SPECTRALVIPER staging DLL 'DtlCrashCatch.dll' being written to disk or image-loaded from anywhere outside System32/WinSxS. ESET names this exact DLL as the side-loaded rogue payload after the FireAnt update chain — and the same DLL name appears in the Vietnamese transport-construction intrusion, so it's a stable IOC across both 2024–2026 OceanLotus clusters. Rationale: DtlCrashCatch.dll is the article's named rogue side-load DLL — extremely high-fidelity string with near-zero benign collisions outside System32/WinSxS. ESET names the same DLL across both the FireAnt cluster and the transport-construction intrusion, confirming it as a stable cross-campaign IOC; Elastic's 2023 write-up describes the same side-loading pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/002/
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1574.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-research VM with the sample copied to %Temp% for analysis (whitelist analyst hostnames)
  • Red-team tooling re-using the DtlCrashCatch.dll name as a tongue-in-cheek IOC test
  • Backup / DFIR collector zipping the DLL into an evidence folder (FileCreated under \Evidence\)
  • Legitimate Acrobat / OneDrive component that happens to ship a same-named DLL in a future build (verify InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("securityresearcher","dfir-collector") and not (FolderPath has @"\Evidence\" or FolderPath has @"\Malware-Analysis\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: SHA1/SHA256 the dropped DLL and compare against the article's SHA1 list (865A1739..., B0FEA981..., 48FEBB91..., 511B7745..., 8CD78B8D...). Check parent process — was it the FireAnt Metakit chain or a different entry point? 2) Contain: network-isolate the host, kill any process with DtlCrashCatch.dll currently loaded (cross-reference DeviceImageLoadEvents → DeviceProcessEvents on InitiatingProcessId), quarantine the DLL file. 3) Hunt: pivot the parent SHA256 (the legit signed binary being abused) across the fleet for other side-load victims; check DeviceNetworkEvents for any subsequent C2 calls to the article's domains.
union
  (DeviceFileEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
   | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
   | where FileName =~ "DtlCrashCatch.dll"
   | where FolderPath !has @"\Windows\System32\" and FolderPath !has @"\Windows\WinSxS\" and FolderPath !has @"\Windows\SysWOW64\"
   | project Timestamp, Source="FileWrite", DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, SHA256,
             InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
             InitiatingProcessAccountName),
  (DeviceImageLoadEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
   | where FileName =~ "DtlCrashCatch.dll"
   | where FolderPath !has @"\Windows\System32\" and FolderPath !has @"\Windows\WinSxS\" and FolderPath !has @"\Windows\SysWOW64\"
   | project Timestamp, Source="ImageLoad", DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, SHA256,
             InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
             InitiatingProcessAccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName)
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "DtlCrashCatch.dll"
| where TargetFilePath !has @"\Windows\System32\" and TargetFilePath !has @"\Windows\WinSxS\" and TargetFilePath !has @"\Windows\SysWOW64\"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName,
          TargetFileSHA1, TargetFileSHA256, EventType, DvcAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: SPECTRALVIPER Side-Load DLL DtlCrashCatch.dll Created In Non-System Path
id: 9b2d8c4a-5e3f-4d6c-b8a1-2c47e9f3a812
description: Detects creation or image-load of DtlCrashCatch.dll outside Windows system directories — the OceanLotus / SPECTRALVIPER side-loading stager named by ESET in the FireAnt Metakit and Vietnamese transport-construction campaigns.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/oceanlotus-hits-vietnam-investors-with.html
  - https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper
author: ThreatHuntingNarwhal
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1574.002
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\DtlCrashCatch.dll'
  filter_legit:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\Windows\System32\'
      - '\Windows\SysWOW64\'
      - '\Windows\WinSxS\'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:(11 OR 7) @TargetFilename:(*\\DtlCrashCatch.dll OR *\\dtlcrashcatch.dll OR *\\DTLCRASHCATCH.DLL)) AND NOT (@TargetFilename:(*\\Windows\\System32\\* OR *\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\* OR *\\Windows\\WinSxS\\*))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\\DtlCrashCatch\.dll$/i
| NOT regex("\\\\Windows\\\\(System32|SysWOW64|WinSxS)\\\\", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="DtlCrashCatch.dll" AND NOT (Filesystem.file_path IN ("*\\Windows\\System32\\*","*\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\*","*\\Windows\\WinSxS\\*")) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_hash Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="DtlCrashCatch.dll" AND NOT (Filesystem.file_path IN ("*\\Windows\\System32\\*","*\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\*","*\\Windows\\WinSxS\\*")) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_hash Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
SPECTRALVIPER injection into OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe AIInstallation High
Detects OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe — abused by SPECTRALVIPER as the injection host — talking to the named C2 infrastructure or any non-Microsoft public destination. Per ESET, DtlCrashCatch.dll injects itself into OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe to launch the backdoor, so subsequent egress from that PID is the injection success signal. Rationale: OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe is the article's named injection target and the C2 domains/IPs come straight from the IOC bundle. Any OneDrive-named process talking to financemachinelearning.com / gatewayrvcenter.com is a definitive SPECTRALVIPER signal — Microsoft's real OneDrive client never resolves either. Note: Sentinel ASIM ImNetworkSession lacks process attribution, so the Sentinel detection falls back to raw Sysmon EID 3 via the Event table where EventData carries both Image and DestinationHostname. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
ATT&CKT1055.001 T1218
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-research lab detonating SPECTRALVIPER sample (whitelist the malware-analysis subnet)
  • Sysmon EventData truncation where Image and DestinationHostname appear in different events — verify with the matching EID 1 process create
  • ProcessName collision if a future malware family also uses the OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe injection host (still high-fidelity given the C2 IPs)
  • Custom OneDrive sync client built in-house and routed through a hosting provider whose IP overlaps an IOC (extremely unlikely)
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the InitiatingProcessSHA256 for the OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe instance — if it differs from a known Microsoft hash, the binary itself was swapped (rare); if Microsoft-signed, the process was injected. Confirm with a DeviceImageLoadEvents query for DtlCrashCatch.dll on the same DeviceId in the prior 1h. 2) Contain: isolate the host, suspend the OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe process (don't kill — memory forensics), block the C2 IPs at perimeter, kill the Metakit.exe parent if still running. 3) Hunt: enumerate every host that resolved/connected to the C2 list in the past 90 days, sweep for DtlCrashCatch.dll, and check public-facing MSSQL servers (the article notes that's the other initial-access vector OceanLotus used).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com")
   or RemoteIP in ("38.60.245.37","139.99.33.239","139.162.11.152","139.180.128.42","142.91.98.77","166.88.77.186","194.68.26.241","103.119.47.104")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessSHA256, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
Event
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Source =~ "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon" and EventID == 3
| where EventData has "OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe"
| where EventData has_any ("financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com","38.60.245.37","139.99.33.239","139.162.11.152","139.180.128.42","142.91.98.77","166.88.77.186","194.68.26.241","103.119.47.104")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, EventID, RenderedDescription, EventData
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: SPECTRALVIPER OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe Beacon To OceanLotus C2
id: 6a7e3f12-9c4b-4d8e-bd71-3f5e9a2c1d04
description: Detects OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe — abused as the SPECTRALVIPER injection host per ESET's OceanLotus FireAnt report — initiating network connections to the named OceanLotus C2 domains or IPs.
references:

author: ThreatHuntingNarwhal
date: 2026/06/17
tags:

logsource:

detection:

  selection_c2:
    - DestinationHostname:

        - 'power-sync-services.com'
        - 'leadingfilipinoteams.com'

        - '139.162.11.152'
        - '139.180.128.42'
        - '142.91.98.77'
        - '166.88.77.186'
        - '194.68.26.241'
